title: Art Direction Without Generic UI
whenToUse: New marketing pages, portfolios, product landing pages, or visual redesigns where a recognizable aesthetic matters.
prerequisites: Know the subject, primary audience, one page goal, and existing brand constraints.
Read current design tokens and brand guidance before proposing replacements.
workflow: Write a one-sentence visual thesis anchored to the product's world, audience, and content.
Explore at least two compositions that differ structurally—not only in accent color. Compare content order, image strategy, type character, density, and signature motif.
Choose 4–6 semantic colors, display/body/utility type roles, spacing rhythm, and one memorable signature detail. Explain why each choice fits.
Compose the hero around the strongest truthful proof: product interface, concrete benefit, relevant visual, or a sharply stated idea.
Build a complete page with realistic content, responsive sections, accessible controls, and a consistent token system.
Run a visual critique pass: remove unearned gradients, random labels, redundant cards, generic stock-like imagery, and any element that does not help comprehension or identity.
hardRules: Do not choose a trendy style just because it is familiar to the model.
Do not ban stylistic tools universally; evaluate whether each belongs to this specific brief.
Do not fabricate product screenshots, metrics, customer logos, reviews, or outcomes.
One strong signature element is usually better than many competing effects.
acceptance: The intended audience and primary action are clear at first glance.
The chosen visual direction has a concise rationale tied to the actual brief.
Typography, composition and content remain coherent at narrow widths.
The result includes visible focus, keyboard support, semantic controls, and a reduced-motion path.
sources: Frontend Design Premium design-context and verification guidance

title: Production Dashboard UX Contract
whenToUse: SaaS/admin dashboards, CRUD screens, settings apps, and any product with repeated workflows or destructive actions.
prerequisites: Inspect DESIGN.md, UX-CONTRACT.md or equivalents; inspect current shared UI primitives and at least one sibling workflow.
Confirm authoritative API, permission and business rules.
workflow: Classify this route as product/admin versus marketing/content; do not force application contracts onto static pages.
Resolve canonical owners for field validation, toast/live region, dialogs, navigation, tables, date/select controls and scroll surfaces.
For each operation, map trigger → pending state → success destination → feedback → failure recovery → focus outcome.
Define default, hover, focus-visible, pressed, selected, disabled, busy, success, warning, error, empty, stale, conflict and permission-changed states as applicable.
Document visual intent in DESIGN.md and behavior in UX-CONTRACT.md only when durable product scope justifies them.
Exercise keyboard, mobile, zoom, error, retry, stale response and permission-revocation behavior; fix shared root causes first.
hardRules: UI hiding is not authorization.
Never silently discard user input or stale filters/sort/page state.
Do not duplicate established behavior in a screen-local component.
Do not claim the static audit proves browser interaction or CRUD correctness.
acceptance: Repeated components have canonical owners.
Form and destructive-action failure recovery is explicit.
The user can always tell what was saved and where an action leads.
Commands and runtime checks actually run, and results are reported exactly.
sources: Frontend Design Premium: interaction contract, async resilience, canonical UI resolution and verification checklist

title: Intentional Motion Choreography
whenToUse: Landing page entrances, dashboard transitions, scroll reveals, shared elements, progressive disclosure, and delightful micro-interactions.
prerequisites: Identify installed animation library and version; use Context7 for current API details.
Decide what motion communicates before writing an animation.
workflow: Choose one motion purpose per interaction: orientation, hierarchy, cause-and-effect, progress, or delight.
Design a timing hierarchy: one lead movement, a short child stagger, then stillness. Define trigger, duration, easing and interruption rules.
Prefer opacity/transform; use layout animation only when the geometry change helps the user track continuity.
Keep content readable and the primary action available while motion runs. Do not gate route access behind decorative animation.
Implement reduced-motion alternatives at a shared configuration/token layer where the library supports it.
Test rapid state changes, interrupted navigation, slow devices, scrolling, resizing and keyboard focus.
hardRules: No fake progress bars.
No scroll hijacking.
No perpetual movement without a meaningful reason.
Do not remove useful state feedback for reduced-motion users.
acceptance: Motion expresses a user-understandable transition.
The page does not shift unpredictably or block interaction.
Reduced-motion and no-hover behavior are usable.
The actual implementation uses current APIs for the installed version.

title: React Motion Implementation Recipe
whenToUse: React apps using Motion/Framer Motion for layout transitions, viewport reveals, shared elements, and gestures.
prerequisites: Check package.json to distinguish `motion/react` from older `framer-motion` imports.
Resolve the installed library version in Context7.
workflow: Define variants at the nearest shared level instead of scattering per-node transition props.
Use `whileInView`/viewport detection only for content that benefits from reveal and make one-shot behavior explicit.
Use stable keys and stable layout identities; scope shared-element IDs to avoid collisions.
Prefer a small number of properties and use transform/opacity for smooth motion.
Set reduced-motion behavior with the API supported by the installed version and preserve non-motion state cues.
Verify SSR/client boundaries, route unmount, list reorder, and preference changes.
hardRules: Never assume old Framer Motion import paths still match the installed package.
Never key a persistent animated entity by array index when items can reorder.
Do not animate every paragraph or card just because the library makes it easy.
acceptance: Imports compile under the installed package.
Animations survive list reorder without identity jumps.
Reduced motion is validated manually or in test.
Interaction can finish or be interrupted without stale UI.

title: Discord Dashboard Foundation
whenToUse: A server-specific Discord bot dashboard with multiple guilds, configuration modules, roles, commands, or analytics.
prerequisites: Separate user login, Discord OAuth scopes, guild membership, bot installation and bot permissions.
Identify server-side authorization contract and secret storage strategy.
workflow: Design a persistent active-guild context and a setup flow that checks bot installation and required permissions.
Group navigation by user tasks, not by backend implementation details. Keep global account/billing separate from guild settings.
Each setting needs an explicit owner, default, schema, server-side permission gate and persisted-save contract.
Prepare disconnected, no-guild, missing-bot, missing-permission, stale-config, rate-limited and save-failed states.
Use visible draft/saved/unsaved states; only show a live preview when it reflects the same normalized schema that is persisted.
Test guild switching during fetch/save, revoked access, retry/idempotency, and mobile navigation.
hardRules: Never ship bot tokens to the browser.
Never trust a guild ID or role ID without checking access server-side.
Never invent statistics or claim config was saved without an API confirmation.
Never request broad permissions without mapping them to product features.
acceptance: Active guild is obvious on every guild-scoped route.
The backend rechecks actor and bot permissions for every write.
All important settings have loading, success, failure and no-access states.
Rate limits and partial API failures are handled explicitly.
sources: Discord official API docs to be checked through Context7/primary docs before code

title: Discord Embed Builder With Truthful Preview
whenToUse: A builder for Discord embeds, buttons, select menus, welcome announcements, or interactive messages.
prerequisites: Confirm the current Discord payload schema and limits through primary documentation.
Define whether preview renders a normalized local payload or a fetched Discord message.
workflow: Model content fields and interactive components with typed schemas.
Validate required fields, string lengths, aggregate limits, URLs, colors and component constraints before enabling save/send.
Keep errors next to the affected control and provide a helpful counter for length-limited fields.
Render a preview from the same normalized payload used by the send API; sanitize rich text and never inject raw HTML.
Prevent duplicate sends and show server-confirmed status, message/link IDs only when actually returned.
Test empty content, limit edges, malformed URLs, permission denial, API rate limit and send failure.
hardRules: Local preview is not proof that Discord accepted the message.
No raw HTML injection.
Do not silently truncate content without showing what changed.
acceptance: Preview maps to payload semantics.
Boundary errors are clear and actionable.
The user can distinguish draft, validated, sending, sent and failed states.
sources: Discord API documentation (verify exact current limits before implementation)

title: Discord Leveling Configuration System
whenToUse: XP rules, level-up messages, rank cards, leaderboards, rewards and manual XP administration.
prerequisites: Define the authoritative XP formula, update cadence, persistence contract and ranking tie-breaker.
Define guild-scoped permissions for manual XP operations and role rewards.
workflow: Use a settings overview with grouped modules rather than a wall of isolated commands.
Design XP curve/threshold controls with example values and explicit units; preview the progression at sample levels.
For role rewards, validate duplicate thresholds, missing roles and bot role hierarchy before save.
Make manual add/remove/reset actions explicit, permission-gated and auditable; confirm bulk/reset-all operations.
Render rank card and leaderboard previews from the same template/data schema used in production.
Test ties, zero/negative values, maximum values, missing avatars, removed users, stale rankings and failed role assignment.
hardRules: Never expose a manual XP mutation without server-side permission checks.
Never claim rank/leaderboard data is live if it is cached or mock data.
Keep one source of truth for level, rank, total XP and progress calculations.
acceptance: XP thresholds are deterministic and tested at boundaries.
Dangerous reset flows require deliberate confirmation.
Preview and production templates agree.
Failure does not leave stale rank/progress UI.
sources: Frontend Design Premium interaction and async resilience guidance

title: Context7-Grounded Implementation
whenToUse: Any project using current libraries/frameworks, especially Next.js, React, Tailwind, Motion, Supabase, MCP, or Discord API integrations.
prerequisites: Know the installed package name/version or be explicit that it is not yet known.
A reliable Context7 tool connection is available in the agent environment.
workflow: Resolve the exact library with Context7; choose the official/high-reputation library ID when several matches exist.
Break the question into narrow independent concepts (e.g. App Router handler and auth) rather than one broad query.
Read docs snippets and note source URL, applicable version, server/client requirements and deprecations.
Write code in the project's established conventions; do not copy unrelated examples verbatim.
Run typecheck/build/tests; compare actual compiler errors with the API docs before iterating.
hardRules: Never use a retrieved snippet as proof that the full project compiles.
Never claim package behavior when the relevant result did not cover it.
If Context7 is unavailable, say so and use official primary documentation instead.
acceptance: Library ID/version fit package.json.
Important API assumptions have cited documentation.
The code is verified in the intended environment or labeled untested.

title: TubeAlfred Video Research to Engineering Notes
whenToUse: When a video tutorial, walkthrough, creator comparison, or real-world build explanation can add useful context.
prerequisites: A specific question that a video can answer.
A way to verify technical details against primary documentation.
workflow: Search YouTube with specific product + concept + intended outcome terms.
Screen publication date, author/channel, topic fit, and whether the video appears educational versus promotional.
Fetch metadata or transcript for only the most relevant few results.
Extract original, concise steps, design tradeoffs, and failure modes; mark transcript uncertainty for exact identifiers or code.
Check package syntax, API limits, security and versioned behavior against official docs such as Context7 results.
Store the original video URL plus summary and a confidence label in the research note.
hardRules: Don't copy transcript passages or present the creator's words as yours.
Views and likes are not technical proof.
Don't use a video as the only source for security-sensitive or version-sensitive implementation.
acceptance: The note answers the specific research question.
Technical claims are cross-checked.
Links, dates and unresolved uncertainty are preserved.

title: Superdesign Canvas Workflow
whenToUse: When using Superdesign to explore a new UI, reproduce an existing page, compare directions, or iterate a design before coding.
prerequisites: Superdesign CLI preflight must run successfully and authentication state must be known.
For an existing codebase, required repo initialization and design-context artifacts must be complete before generation.
workflow: Run the documented CLI preflight and inspect its auth/project output.
Classify the target: existing rendered UI, new target in existing codebase, or brand-new project.
For a real codebase, initialize and inspect the current design context; do not generate before the init gate completes.
Create a design brief with subject, audience, primary task, existing constraints, reference scope, and one signature element.
Generate independent structural variants only when comparison is useful; use iteration mode to refine a chosen direction.
Read actual canvas/preview URLs from tool output and wait for user approval before implementation unless the user explicitly says to skip design.
hardRules: Never fabricate project, draft, node or canvas identifiers.
Do not run design-generation commands before required initialization.
If CLI is not available, disclose it and do not claim a canvas was created.
acceptance: The correct target workflow was selected.
The chosen visual direction has a clear rationale.
The user receives a real canvas URL only if the command returned one.
sources: Installed Superdesign skill and its workflow references

title: Superpowers Engineering Loop
whenToUse: Multi-step code changes, tricky bugs, new integrations, security-sensitive work, or reusable feature systems.
prerequisites: An outcome and acceptance criteria are known.
A shell/test environment or an honest limitation statement is available.
workflow: Brainstorm enough to settle user goals, constraints and meaningful design alternatives.
Write a stepwise plan with exact paths, interfaces, and commands/tests.
For behavior, follow red → green → refactor: demonstrate the failing test before the fix.
Implement the smallest coherent slice; split tasks by independent interfaces when parallelism actually helps.
Review specification compliance first, then code quality and maintainability.
Run verification commands and record observed output; do not infer success from intent.
hardRules: Do not write a large speculative diff before settling the design.
Do not skip a red test step and still call the work TDD.
Do not claim commands ran unless their results were observed.
acceptance: Plan tasks are executable and testable.
Regression behavior is covered by evidence.
Code matches the plan and is reviewed.
Final status separates completed, unverified and blocked items.

title: MCP Tool Contracts and Safety
whenToUse: Adding a tool to a remote MCP server, defining its input schema, exposing repository actions or integrating third-party APIs.
prerequisites: Know the MCP transport and SDK version.
Classify the tool as read-only, write, privileged or destructive.
workflow: Give each tool one focused capability with clear title, description, input schema and structured output.
Validate untrusted inputs server-side and enforce authorization where the action is performed.
Return actionable, bounded results; distinguish empty/not-found, validation errors and upstream failures.
Make write tools idempotent when possible and require explicit confirmation for irreversible operations.
Test initialize, list tools, invalid params, normal success, upstream error, timeout and authorization-denied scenarios.
Document which connected MCP/provider supplies external deployment or code-editing actions.
hardRules: A public unauthenticated server must not expose private-data reads or privileged mutations.
Do not imply that a plan-generating tool has edited code or deployed an app.
Never pass secrets back in tool results or logs.
acceptance: Schema rejects malformed inputs.
Tool behavior matches its description.
Access controls exist at the action boundary.
A real protocol handshake and representative tool call are tested.
sources: MCP and Vercel deployment guidance; verify exact SDK API through Context7

title: Accessible Interaction Audit
whenToUse: Before release or after changing buttons, navigation, dialog, forms, tables, responsive controls or animation.
prerequisites: Know target browsers and relevant accessibility requirements.
Have access to the rendered page where possible.
workflow: Exercise every action with keyboard only; confirm visible focus and predictable order.
Check semantic button/link/control roles and accessible names; ensure invalid fields reference visible errors.
Inspect contrast, text zoom/reflow, touch target size and whether sticky UI obscures focus.
Test dialog open/close, focus trap/restoration, Escape behavior and nested interactions.
Enable reduced motion and check that state cues and functionality remain.
Separate static findings from runtime checks and report repro steps with severity.
hardRules: No clickable div/span when a real button/link fits.
No color-only status or icon-only unlabeled controls.
No inaccessible drag-only interaction without an alternative.
acceptance: Keyboard-only path completes core task.
Focus, names, errors and contrast are checked.
Reduced-motion and narrow layouts remain functional.
Findings map to observable evidence.
sources: Frontend Design Premium interaction contract and verification checklist

title: Research Evidence Ledger
whenToUse: Cross-source research, design-system decisions, package/version decisions, and recommendations that may be stale.
prerequisites: A concrete question and candidate sources.
workflow: Split opinion, design inspiration and technical facts into separate claim types.
Use primary docs for APIs, official product docs for product capabilities, Context7 for versioned library evidence, and TubeAlfred for tutorial context.
Record the publication/update date when recency matters and prefer evidence matching the requested timeframe.
Keep contradictory evidence visible and state which source is authoritative for which claim.
Attach confidence and an explicit follow-up test for unresolved questions.
hardRules: Don't cite a video for API truth when current docs are available.
Don't hide uncertainty or infer a missing version.
Don't turn a popularity signal into proof.
acceptance: Each material claim can be traced to evidence.
Freshness and version are preserved.
Uncertainty and unresolved conflicts are visible.

title: Author High-Signal Agent Skills
whenToUse: Creating, expanding, or revising a reusable skill catalogue or agent instruction set.
prerequisites: A clearly bounded skill trigger and user outcome.
A plan for evaluating whether the skill changes output quality.
workflow: Choose a precise title, trigger condition, and outcome; avoid skills that restate 'do good work'.
Write a workflow with specific decisions, artifacts, ordering and failure paths.
Include anti-patterns and boundary cases, not just aspirational principles.
Define observable acceptance checks plus explicit conditions that should stop or escalate the task.
Separate stable principles from versioned API facts; direct agents to Context7/primary docs for current syntax.
Test on at least two representative prompts and one adversarial or edge-case prompt; revise when the skill produces generic or contradictory behavior.
hardRules: Do not count thin topic labels as equivalent to high-quality skills.
Do not clone third-party skill text; synthesize reusable original instructions and preserve source attribution.
Do not claim evaluation passed without running examples.
acceptance: Skill contains trigger, workflow, guardrails, outputs and checks.
Its guidance is specialized and not interchangeable with sibling skills.
Its behavior can be evaluated with concrete test prompts.
sources: Frontend Design Premium structure and evidence-first verification
